EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the typical pattern of an alkyl-para-disubstituted benzene:  
• Two very strong C-H out–of–plane bending bands at 811 / 825 cm⁻¹, characteristic of p-disubstituted rings.  
• An intense ring-breathing band at 970 cm⁻¹, expected for para-dialkyl benzenes.  
• Aromatic C=C stretch at 1621 cm⁻¹ and strong aromatic C–H stretches at 3022–3057 cm⁻¹.  
• Multiple aliphatic C–H stretches at 2879–2972 cm⁻¹ and CH₃/CH₂ deformation bands at 1450 and 1382 cm⁻¹, indicating alkyl groups but no heteroatom-bound hydrogens (no O–H or N–H stretch).  
Among the candidates, only 1 (CCc1ccc(C)cc1) is a para-dialkylbenzene (p-ethyl-toluene) that fits all these features and has no heteroatoms that would introduce additional strong bands (e.g., C=O or C–O) absent in the experiment.
